rows.basis: Revenue of the Intelligent Infrastructure segment (cloud, data center infrastructure, networking, capital equipment) is 17.872B of 35.954B total. It is a data-center line, not a pure AI one, because it also includes capital equipment and non-AI networking. Regulated Industries and Connected Living & Digital Commerce are excluded. The MD&A ties growth to 'certain AI infrastructure programs'. The thesis records a call figure of about $14.4B AI-related revenue, which is not in the pack and is not used here.

Revenue of the Intelligent Infrastructure segment is 12.317B of 29.802B total. The MD&A says the segment grew 34%, driven by cloud and data center infrastructure (+30%) and capital equipment (+10%). Capital equipment and non-AI networking are included, so this overstates AI. The other two segments are excluded.

Revenue of the Intelligent Infrastructure segment is 9.197B of 28.883B total. The pack carries the same value under two capitalisations and it is counted once. The CEO cites growth in the 'AI datacenter space' in words only. The segment includes capital equipment and non-AI networking.

Revenue of the Intelligent Infrastructure segment is 11.072B of 34.702B total. This is a broad data-center, networking and capital-equipment line from before the AI ramp, and no AI statement covers this year. The other segments are excluded.

The release cites 'accelerating AI demand' within a total FY2027 revenue outlook of $44.5B. That total covers the whole business and is not the AI part. The thesis records a call figure of about $22.1B in AI-related revenue expected for FY2027, which is not in the pack.
The FY2025 release names 'AI data center infrastructure' as a significant opportunity ahead. It gives no amount.
